knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says the rate is built from your own costs and billable hours, so the work that can be billed recovers the costs and income. Using all paid hours, a competitor's rate or a wished-for rate does not do this.
The lesson says travel and set-up time does not shrink with the length of the cut, so a minimum charge covers the time needed to reach the client. It does not replace a written quote for every visit.

The lesson says to use your own costs and billable hours first, then compare with local evidence from your bookings and chosen benchmarks. A single national average, a friend's rate or one bidding-site price is not a sound check.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-month log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Estimate the paid working hours in a year, then subtract travel, admin, marketing, training and leave to find the billable hours.
